bull_bear.body:
- Net debt free; net cash ₹1,276 mn (31-Mar-26).
- Dividend 20% (₹2/share) declared; investor pushed for sustained ≥20% payout, mgmt receptive.
- Inorganic growth a stated strategy — actively scouting US, Europe, India; nothing material to announce. Reinvesting profits.
- Possible Alucast demerger/divestment under consideration (no decision).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitics repeatedly flagged: West Asia war, oil/petroleum shortage, tariffs, lockdown "rumors" — all guidance caveated on "normal working."
- Alucast still PAT-negative (-₹41 mn FY26); turnaround depends on long qualification cycles; double-digit margin pushed to FY28. Demerger uncertainty.
- Solar: not yet cost-competitive vs Chinese mass-manufacturing in India ("close, but not for profit"); no government support that China enjoys; US requires full UL re-design (slow lab queues); Europe solar declining (pivoting to Middle East).
- US data-center timing risk: if products/certifications arrive late, relegated to replacement market.
- FX: euro/PLN-INR translation skews reported Polish numbers; rupee at ₹85 noted.
- OEM-vs-own-brand channel conflict in solar (mgmt downplays).
- Investor pushback that US growth ($3→4.5 mn, ~₹12-13 cr increment) is "underachievement" given portfolio.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, candid and granular. Beat their own FY26 EBITDA guidance (₹110 cr → ₹126/136 cr) and acknowledged it explicitly. Honest on weaknesses — solar not yet China-competitive, US growth modest, Alucast still loss-making at PAT level. Backed Alucast recovery with "concrete data, not wishful thinking" (offers given, audits cleared, negotiations). Promoter (Goliya) added dividend and demerger color directly. Repeated explicit geopolitical caveats — neither over-promising nor alarmist.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **CTs are the quiet data-center & grid play:** "one product goes behind every meter in every data center," UL-certified, capacity +67% (6k→10k/day) — most concrete monetization of the AI-capex theme, not the headline solar story.
- **Lumel SA is the profit engine, not India:** 51% of group PAT from a "subdued" European market — group quality hinges on Poland electronics, with EU-funded SMT line as a moat for SIL-rated MV controllers.
- **Alucast is the swing factor:** the entire 161% EBITDA jump largely came from plugging Alucast's ₹150 mn loss, not organic EEI alone — FY27 growth must come from EEI as Alucast goes flat (one-time benefit won't repeat).
- **Solar is optionality, not a thesis:** ₹24-25 cr FY27 on lower (15-20% GM) margins; mgmt itself frames it as a "bamboo tree" just sprouting; hybrid + Middle East/Saudi export is the real call option.
- **US acquisition is being actively explored** specifically to beat the data-center certification clock — potential inorganic catalyst.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - Disciplined capital allocation is listed among management's stated FY27 priorities, alongside profitable growth, better product mix, new product development, deeper customer relationships and strategic geographic expansion; no dividend, payout ratio or balance-sheet specifics are given.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Highly vertically integrated, largely in-house manufacturing model providing control over quality, cost and delivery
- Broad diversification -- over 200 product groups sold in 100+ countries through 360+ distributors, reducing dependence on any single product, customer, geography or industry cycle
- Integrated hardware + software offering via the Microsys PROMOTIC SCADA platform, enabling a move from standalone product supply to end-to-end monitoring, control and energy-visibility solutions
- Established international route-to-market platforms -- Sifam Tinsley (UK/US) and Lumel SA (Poland) -- providing local presence, distribution, inventory and customer support in developed markets
- Group-level sourcing and SAP/SAP HANA-enabled operational visibility supporting tighter cost control, lower inventory ratios and shorter lead times
- In-house R&D and engineering across global centres aligned as a unified innovation engine, supporting a five-year product development pipeline
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical risk — Operations and exports may be influenced by global economic trends, geopolitical developments, trade-related uncertainty and regional market volatility, which can affect demand, pricing and profitability; mitigated by diversifying market presence across geographies and maintaining cost control and customer diversification.
- Sectoral exposure, particularly automotive — Prolonged challenges in certain end-use industries, particularly automotive, may affect order volumes and profitability (relevant to the HPDC/Lumel Alucast business); the Company is improving customer/contract mix and reviewing legacy contracts to raise business quality.
- Input cost and currency risk — Volatility in raw material costs, energy prices and exchange rates can impact overall cost structures and margins; mitigated via long-term supply arrangements, operational efficiency and pricing measures.
- Technology and innovation risk — Evolving customer needs and rapid technological change may affect product relevance and competitiveness; addressed through continued R&D investment, new product development and technology partnerships.
- Project execution risk — Expansion-related delays or execution challenges in manufacturing facilities (e.g. the Nashik expansion) may affect production capacity and growth plans; managed by phased project planning and regular reviews.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — Operating across multiple jurisdictions requires adherence to diverse regulatory frameworks, product certifications and compliance requirements; managed via dedicated compliance teams, periodic audits and certifications.
- Supply chain risk — Supply chain disruptions may affect availability of key components, production timelines and cost efficiencies; mitigated by strengthening supplier networks, inventory planning and in-house manufacturing capabilities where feasible.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Standalone Rishabh (India):** consistent performer; high-margin export wins; largest CT maker globally by value/volume — 6,000 CTs/day, expanding to 10,000/day.
- **Lumel SA (Poland):** 51% of group PAT, 23%+ EBITDA. Commissioned one of Europe's most advanced SMT/electronics assembly lines (40% funded by EU; for next-gen complex MV controllers, SIL 1/SIL 2). Does MV protection relays/controllers.
- **Lumel Alucast (Polish HPDC):** planned shrink — exited ~₹100 cr of loss-making legacy auto contracts (₹250 cr → ₹180 cr business). Cut from 3 shifts to 2; turnaround real but FY27 is volume-rebuild year. Possible demerger floated by investor — mgmt: "a possibility, no decision."
- **STI USA/UK, V&A China:** all EBITDA-positive, fast growth on small base. Microsys (software) acquired to bundle solutions for data centers.

business.body:

latest_quarter.body:
- FY26 gross margin 554 bps higher at 54% (vs 48.6%) on product mix + buying diversification/efficiency, employee & other costs in check.
- Product contribution margins span 20% (solar, EMS) to 60-70% (power-quality analyzers); blended EEI EBITDA ~24% in FY26 but mgmt deliberately conservative, guiding 20-22% because richer-mix solar volume can dilute %.
- EEI passes through input cost increases (own brand/products/pricing). Energy-efficiency products are counter-cyclical to high European energy prices (ISO 50001 / ESG compliance demand).
- Alucast hampered structurally by European labour/energy costs; mgmt argues many EU competitors have closed → projects shifting to survivors + dual-sourcing trend supports recovery.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
**This quarter (Q4/FY26):**
- Consol EBITDA margin Q4 16.2% (+760 bps YoY); FY26 16.3% (+960 bps). PAT +292% FY26.
- Beat self-set ₹110 cr FY26 EBITDA guidance (₹126 cr reported / ₹136 cr adj).
- Lumel Alucast turned adj-EBITDA positive (+₹33 mn vs -₹150 mn) — main driver of group jump; still PAT-negative.
- Dividend reinstated/declared at 20% (₹2/share).
- Nashik 2-facility expansion completed, under commissioning (capacity ~2x).
- Lumel SA SMT line commissioned (40% EU-funded).
- Solar iUNO single-phase launched, turned unit-profitable; ₹24-25 cr FY27 target.
- US revenue $3 mn (+50% YoY); CT capacity expansion 6k→10k/day underway.

**Next-quarter / FY27 watch items:**
- Verify EEI 20-25% growth & 20-22% EBITDA materializing in Q1 FY27.
- Nashik facilities full commissioning by June/July — watch ramp.
- Solar inverter ₹24-25 cr trajectory + hybrid launch + OEM deals.
- Alucast: new RFQ conversions, flat top-line (~₹180 cr constant currency), no-loss confirmation; demerger decision.
- US: $4.5 mn target, possible US acquisition announcement, new UL-certified products.
- MV VT/PT design completion by end-FY27 (sales FY28).
- Geopolitics / oil / FX (euro-PLN-INR) impact on reported numbers.

outlook.body:
- **EEI segment FY27: 20-25% top-line growth (anchored ~20%), EBITDA 20-22%.** Same guideline as last year (which they beat). Rishabh standalone & Lumel SA (~85% of EEI) each ~20%; smaller STI/V&A (~13-15%) ~30%.
- **Solar inverters FY27: ~₹24-25 cr (roughly doubling).** US business FY27: $4.5 mn (+~40-50% off $3 mn), aspiration ₹100 cr in 3-4 yrs.
- **Lumel Alucast FY27: flat-to-slightly-lower vs ₹238 cr (target ~₹180 cr constant currency), no losses, no growth.** Double-digit margin only in FY28, not FY27.
- **Medium-voltage VT/PT products: design ready by end-FY27, sales from FY28.**
- **FY28 aspiration (in response to investor):** "close to" ₹1,000 cr revenue & ~₹150-160 cr adj EBITDA — mgmt would not firmly commit to ₹1,000 cr crossing.
- *Next-quarter (Q1 FY27) explicit number: none given — guidance is annual.*
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body:
- No consolidated order-book figure disclosed (B2B instrumentation, book-and-ship). Demand described as "healthy, sustainable" across export and domestic, "strong order pipeline."
- Alucast: multiple RFQs in progress; a few approved, several in price/T&C negotiation — ~3-4 new customers + 2-3 new projects from existing customers; volumes land "order booking + 1 year" (i.e., FY28).
- Data-center: won + repeat projects from Sify (India); similar in UK supporting Ireland; developing US-specific products.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Medium-voltage expansion:** CTs already released; MV protection relays (Lumel) + CTs (Rishabh) live; VT/PT design ready end-FY27. No high-voltage intent ("too diverse").
- **Solar inverters:** iUNO single-phase (≤10 kW) launched Q3-Q4 FY25 with strong response; NEO 3-phase up to 50 kW; now operationally/unit profitable (gross margins 15-20%, lower than core). Hybrid single-phase in development → opens Middle East / Saudi / Europe export. Dual go-to-market: own brand + OEM supply to Indian brands that currently assemble Chinese SKDs. New Nashik floor can scale solar to ~₹100 cr with incremental assembly lines.
- **Data centers / AI capex:** CTs behind every meter (UL-certified) is a key US growth driver; bundling products + Microsys software; exploring US acquisition to fast-track certification and "catch at least half" of the 5-6 yr capex wave before it becomes replacement-only.
- **EMS / semicon (PLI-linked):** doing complex assemblies incl. laptop motherboards (a former-Intel-principal customer); cam switches a planned new line.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scale product ranges where global demand is strongest: solar inverters, current transformers, MID meters, energy management systems and medium-voltage products
- Extend the product basket through in-house, world-class R&D across global centres aligned as one unified innovation engine
- Strategically increase presence in high-growth markets: Latin America, Mexico, Canada, Southeast Asia and Africa
- Actively evaluate acquisitions both in India and abroad to add complementary capabilities to the electrical and electronic instruments portfolio
- Move from standalone product supply to higher-value, integrated monitoring and automation solutions by combining hardware with the Microsys PROMOTIC SCADA software layer
- Reposition the High Pressure Die Casting (Lumel Alucast) business towards better contract quality, cost discipline and a more balanced mix across end-use sectors, reducing dependence on low-margin automotive contracts and increasing non-automotive and EV-agnostic applications
- Aggressively scale the integrated 'measure-monitor-convert-optimise' solution set (Radius solar conversion + SCADA monitoring) into the US, Europe and other priority geographies
- Build a scalable manufacturing platform via the Nashik expansion (two new multi-storeyed buildings) for next-generation instrumentation and electronics capacity
- Leverage group-level sourcing and cross-selling across the diversified global platform (200+ product groups, 100+ countries, 360+ distributors) to unlock wider markets
- The Board proposed a final dividend of Rs 2 per equity share (face value Rs 10) for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the 43rd AGM. The Board decided to retain the entire profit for FY 2025-26 in the statement of profit and loss, with no transfer to reserves. IPO proceeds continue to be utilised for the purposes stated in the Prospectus, with the unutilised portion held in bank deposits pending deployment.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Rishabh is executing a manufacturing expansion at Nashik, adding two new multi-storeyed buildings intended to more than double production capacity over the next three to four years across solar inverters, medium-voltage products, energy management systems, MID meters and other scalable product ranges. At Lumel Alucast (Poland, HPDC), the Company installed a new 1.5 MW solar installation as part of an energy-cost-reduction initiative during its turnaround from losses to breakeven, and is now working to fill available capacity with profitable contracts already at advanced stages of negotiation, targeting securing them in FY 2026-27 and launching in FY 2027-28. On the process side, the Company moved Resin Cast Current Transformer manufacturing to a gravity-casting process, tripling output quantity versus the old process with zero casting rejection and enhancing capacity to 1000 CTs per day. The F-31 Plant also had a 280 KW solar power system installed as an alternate-energy initiative alongside automation-based energy controls (motion sensors, AC auto-switch-off units, a Shop Electrical Shutdown Monitoring System).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Long-term investment cycle remains supported by structural trends -- electrification, industrial automation, energy efficiency, grid modernization and renewable energy integration -- expected to sustain demand for intelligent electrical monitoring, automation, testing & measurement and energy management solutions globally, even as near-term demand stays steady amid macro/geopolitical uncertainty
- India remains a high-growth domestic market and competitive global manufacturing hub, with infrastructure investment, the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme and renewable/rooftop-solar buildout driving demand across the Company's EEI, Test & Measurement, Solar Inverters and Precision Die Casting businesses
- Europe continues to invest in energy efficiency, grid modernisation, renewable integration, automation and industrial productivity despite modest regional growth, remaining relevant to Rishabh's measurement, monitoring, control, testing and energy management products
- Rising global industrial automation (robot installations above 500,000 units for a fourth consecutive year), semiconductor sales growth and data-centre power demand growth are increasing the criticality of testing and power-monitoring requirements, supporting the Portable Test & Measurement and power-network monitoring portfolios
- Global renewable power capacity is expected to grow by almost 4,600 GW between 2025 and 2030 with solar PV representing nearly 80% of the expansion, supporting demand for the Radius solar inverter range
- HPDC segment's revenue share was deliberately reduced to 30.7% of FY26 revenue from 36.6% in FY25 as the Company shifts away from lower-margin automotive business toward improved contract quality
- Lumel SA (Poland) secured a EUR 5 million contract in the German energy sector during FY26
- Rishabh has executed two Data Centre Infrastructure Monitoring projects for a Fortune India 500 company, with a third, larger project currently in progress
- Lumel Alucast has multiple contracts at advanced stages of negotiation, with priority on securing these projects in FY 2026-27 and launching them in FY 2027-28
- Solar India business recorded 8% revenue growth and 192% volume growth in FY 2025-26, reflecting early traction in the Radius solar-conversion business
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

risks.note: Operations and exports may be influenced by global economic trends, geopolitical developments, trade-related uncertainty and regional market volatility, which can affect demand, pricing and profitability; mitigated by diversifying market presence across geographies and maintaining cost control and customer diversification.

Prolonged challenges in certain end-use industries, particularly automotive, may affect order volumes and profitability (relevant to the HPDC/Lumel Alucast business); the Company is improving customer/contract mix and reviewing legacy contracts to raise business quality.

Volatility in raw material costs, energy prices and exchange rates can impact overall cost structures and margins; mitigated via long-term supply arrangements, operational efficiency and pricing measures.

Evolving customer needs and rapid technological change may affect product relevance and competitiveness; addressed through continued R&D investment, new product development and technology partnerships.

Expansion-related delays or execution challenges in manufacturing facilities (e.g. the Nashik expansion) may affect production capacity and growth plans; managed by phased project planning and regular reviews.

Operating across multiple jurisdictions requires adherence to diverse regulatory frameworks, product certifications and compliance requirements; managed via dedicated compliance teams, periodic audits and certifications.

Supply chain disruptions may affect availability of key components, production timelines and cost efficiencies; mitigated by strengthening supplier networks, inventory planning and in-house manufacturing capabilities where feasible.
